title: Niece Hocile's records and how alike they sang
summary: They sorted out records credited to her but sung by Hocile, who was raised with her and died around 1940.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: How did you like those tunes we just played?
Fine. I loved every one of them.

That's very interesting that you said it was ______. It was "Dead Drunk Blues," "Have You Ever Been Drunk?", "Lazy Man Blues," and "You're Going to Need My Help," because Brian Rust (PHONETIC) ______, they're all attributed to you, but you say they were your niece, Hocile (PHONETIC).
Uh-huh.
You both sang very much alike.
Yeah, we do sing alike, uh-huh.
But you said she was younger than you?
(Unintelligible) about two years. I may not be two, but about two, because --
How is it you sang so much alike?
Because we was raised together. (Unintelligible) my sister. Mama raised both of us.
So you both learned the songs together?
Yeah, (unintelligible).
Uh-huh. You had no trouble recognizing which was yours and which was hers.
____ was the heavy, only thing was the heavy, the heaviness, you know. And of course, I know Herschel's playing, you know. But I played that 'Mighty Tight Woman' myself.
That was you playing on that one, 'Mighty Tight Woman?'
Uh-huh.
Yeah. That's good to know, because we're going to correct the records now. When did she die? Hocile?
She must have died in -- Queenie in '34 and I think ____ was 70 when she died. (Inaudible). She's been dead quite a while. She must have died -- let me
see. (Inaudible). (Unintelligible) didn't even put no down (unintelligible). It must have been about '40.
About 1940?
Uh-huh.
